# Spar 0.6.3

**A challenge that failed validation used to be thrown away and written again
from scratch, fifteen times, while you watched. Now it gets repaired. 0.6.3 also
stops asking for Big-O after challenges that were never about it, puts your
message on screen the moment you send it, and rebuilds the menus so hovering
does not have to wait for an animation to finish.**

## The challenge gets fixed instead of rewritten

- **One authoring call per turn, repaired in place.** A candidate rejected for
  one failing test used to come back as a wholly new statement, reference,
  starter and test suite — because the only move available was to start over.
  The compiler owns the error and the rejected input is the closest thing to a
  source tree, so both now stay where they are: the repair returns only the
  fields that must change, and file maps merge by path.
- **Four repairs, then the fallback.** Bounded on purpose. The validator is not
  allowed to become a second agent loop.
- **A rejected revision leaves your challenge alone.** There was already a valid
  challenge on screen, and the generic fallback used to overwrite it. Spar says
  the revision did not make it and leaves the work standing.

## Big-O only where Big-O is the point

- **The challenge says whether it is an efficiency exercise.** Syntax, debugging,
  refactoring, repository mechanics — all of them were being asked for asymptotic
  time and auxiliary space after a pass, where the answer is either trivial or
  meaningless.
- **Two gates, two owners.** The agent decides whether complexity is useful
  evidence for this challenge; the Settings switch decides whether Spar may
  interrupt a solve for it at all. One function combines them, so submitting,
  restoring, reviewing and acknowledging cannot drift apart.
- **Challenges written before this exists are not guessed at.** Only an explicit
  yes opens the checkpoint.

## The thread

- **Your message appears when you send it.** It used to wait on persistence and
  agent startup, so the composer emptied into nothing.
- **"Thinking" stops piling up.** Provider reasoning was being filed into the
  transcript, which stranded old thinking rows above later prose and tool calls,
  as though the model had gone back to think again. One loader at the live edge,
  nothing once settled.
- **Code blocks have a header** — language, glyph, copy — and stay readable while
  they are still streaming.
- **One type size.** The thread was one size in the stylesheet and two on screen.
  The rule compiled correctly and was silently never applied; a heading in a
  reply was a third size arriving mid-column. Headings are weight and space now.

## The workspace

- **One run signal.** The busy rim is off the editor. That is where you are
  looking and typing, and a breathing edge around it is where the signal becomes
  a distraction. The run is reported on the panel that reports runs.
- **The complexity card waits for the verdict.** It used to slide in over the
  result still landing, asking for Big-O before you had read whether you passed.

## Menus

- **Hover comes first and the animation second.** Moving down a list beside an
  open submenu used to light up nothing for a third of a second, and a fast sweep
  across providers spent its whole trip stuck. Rows answer to the pointer
  directly; the diagonal into an open submenu is protected by an actual triangle.
- **Switching submenus does not animate.** No more two popups fading past each
  other.
- **The surfaces are rebuilt** — geometry, glass, rim and shadow — and Select had
  no open animation at all, which is now fixed.
- **Model and Effort have shortcuts.** Shift-Cmd-M and Shift-Cmd-period, named in
  their tooltips.

## Around it

- **Fast mode**, for models served on OpenAI's priority tier, in the effort menu
  under its own heading.
- **The kind of work the next problem is** — a diagnosis, a prerequisite, a
  transfer — named and coloured on the home card, instead of "NEXT UP".
- **An eval harness**, running against the same turn payload the app sends, so a
  measurement of the agent is a measurement of the product.
- **The OpenAI mark takes the row's own colour** rather than a brand green
  nothing else uses.

## Saved problems and tracks

- Save generated and connected-provider problems to a persistent library, with bookmarks shared between problem cards and the thread.
- Remove a track together with its sessions from the Tracks page.

## Clearer teaching and tool details

- Challenge handoffs explain why the problem follows from the learner's evidence.
- Published challenges and solve replays have dedicated cards, including replay statistics and a preview of the learner's code.
- Solution previews reuse the editor's file tabs and background. Tool content inherits the thread's font size, and expanded panels keep their borders visible.
- Attempt events use a compact timeline with aligned timestamps.
- Challenge cards use the editor background while retaining their existing border and hover behavior.

## Settings navigation

- Search settings and jump directly to a section, with a section rail for longer pages.
- Refine settings surfaces, tooltip shadows, and inline-code spacing.
